title: q-completely monotonic and q-Bernstein functions
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18683v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For $0<q><1$, we study (q)-completely monotone and q-Bernstein functions defined by the Jackson derivative. We establish the positive linear closure of the latter class and prove an integral characterization of q-Bernstein functions continuous at zero on a geometric lattice. The representing measures satisfy the natural L\'evy integrability condition, and the corresponding integral kernels are positive semidefinite. We prove that classical completely monotone and Bernstein functions belong to the respective q-classes and examine composition with absolutely monotone functions. Explicit examples show the limits of product closure, composition, and definiteness with respect to ordinary addition.

title: Quaternionic Wave Numbers and the Dirac Equation: Resolving the Nielsen--Ninomiya Barrier and Infinities
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18691v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We exemplify the applicability of the rational wave numbers by formulating the relativistic Dirac equation on the discrete sequence space $\mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}$ over the quaternions $\mathbb{H}$ and demonstrating how this resolves fundamental issues relating to Dirac's equation. Generating $\mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}$ from the primitive basis $\mathcal{P}_0 = \{E_Z, E_{\bar{1}}\}$ as both a static closure and a dynamic enumeration, we show that coupling local quantum kinematics with global cosmological expansion leads to the following results: (1) Dirac 4-spinors and the Clifford algebra $\mathrm{C}\ell_{1,3}(\mathbb{R})$ emerge from the second Cayley--Dickson doubling (biquaternions $\mathbb{H} \otimes \mathbb{C}$); (2) under dynamic generation on an integer clock lattice with causal horizon $\Lambda_m$, relativistic difference operators require temporal depth, establishing clock beat $m = 2$ as the universal Matter Genesis Threshold; (3) the Nielsen--Ninomiya fermion doubling barrier is circumvented on modular sequences $\mathbb{Z}/Q\mathbb{Z}$ because candidate zone-edge doubler modes ($p = Q/2$) are actively pruned at the generational boundary by the coprime sieve projector $\mathcal{S}_Q$ ($\gcd(Q/2, Q) > 1$), preserving exact chiral symmetry without Wilson terms; (4) the discrete fermionic Green's function $S_Q(n, m)$ possesses no coincident-point singularity ($n = m$), converting ultraviolet loop integrals into finite Dedekind and Kloosterman character sums, realizing Dirac's demand for an infinity-free theory; and (5) Zitterbewegung is resolved as an observable stroboscopic beat against vacuum reference $E_Z$, identifying rest mass $m_0$ as a vacuum coupling beat frequency for stationary periodic cycles on the saturated quotient graph.

title: Generalized particle systems: a locality-factorized metamodel for self-propelled particles and agent-based models
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18709v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a single formal object, the generalized particle system (GPS), under which self-propelled particle systems (SPPS) and agent-based models (ABMs) are instances of one construction. A GPS is a typed finite population, a per-particle state space with arbitrary internal structure, a global environment, a neighbourhood map that may depend on the configuration, and type-indexed local rules; these assemble into a generator whose iteration is a monoid action, i.e. an autonomous dynamical system. Update schedules and stochastic rules are added at the same generality, so sequential and noisy models (the original Primordial Particle System, Vicsek) are covered, not approximated. The construction isolates the one ingredient separating the two communities: in the classical ABM reading the dependency graph is fixed; in an SPPS it is a function of the state. Under an exchangeability axiom (rules see neighbours only through the multiset of their types and states) the generator is equivariant for type-preserving permutations and descends to a dynamical system on counting measures, the setting of kinetic limits of swarming models. We read the tuple as a metamodel: its structural components coordinatize a space of models inside which numerical parameters live. Six pre-registered experiments on one engine implementing the generator test the claims: freezing the neighbourhood map destroys alignment ($\varphi = 0.91 \to 0.04$) while yielding a different, non-aligned aggregation; the realized neighbourhood graph rewires up to 64% of its edges per step, its rewiring rate anti-correlated with order ($-0.99$); a topological instead of metric neighbourhood reshapes a flocking phase diagram; the same rule with cohesion and separation off shows a Vicsek-type transition whose susceptibility peak grows with system size. One prediction failed and one subsumption claim is unconfirmed; both are reported.

title: A Las Vegas algorithm for satisfiable SAT formulas, with an application to timetabling
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18720v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many scheduling problems need many different feasible timetables, and a view of how much freedom each event has. We study a Las Vegas algorithm that samples satisfying assignments of a Boolean formula one variable at a time: it draws each value from an estimate of its conditional probability, propagates, and restarts on a contradiction. Every output is a checked solution and comes with the exact probability of producing it. We prove that a run succeeds with probability at least $2^{-K}$, where $K$ is the expected Kullback--Leibler divergence between the true and estimated conditional probabilities along the run of a uniform solution. We also bound the distance of the outputs from uniform from the samples alone; it is a divergence in the opposite direction to $K$, so a sampler can succeed more often while being farther from uniform. On generated timetabling instances counted exactly, belief propagation on the timetabling problem brings $K$ to at most about one bit, and the estimated counts are within 2% of the exact ones. On a real university instance of the International Timetabling Competition 2019, rerunning only the failed runs delivered all 72 requested timetables with each of two estimators. Belief propagation succeeds in 31% of runs. Steered by a Markov chain that carries a nearly feasible timetable, it succeeds in 65% of runs, with outputs at least 300 bits from uniform. There the importance weights are too uneven to estimate the number of timetables, and we certify a lower bound instead. For random 3-SAT, an estimator whose $K$ grows logarithmically would give a polynomial-time Las Vegas algorithm beyond the densities at which any algorithm is proved to succeed; we conjecture that one exists below the satisfiability threshold.

title: The Maximum Number of Sets for 16 Cards is 26
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18722v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In SET, each card has four properties with three values each, and three cards form a \emph{set} when every property is all the same or all different. We prove that the maximum number of sets among $13$, $14$, $15$, and $16$ cards is $16$, $19$, $23$, and $26$, respectively. Viewing cards as points of $\mathbb{F}_3^4$ and sets as lines, we show that a configuration that leaves one of the $40$ line directions of $\mathbb{F}_3^4$ unused projects into $\mathbb{F}_3^3$ without losing a set, which reduces the problem to three properties, where exhaustive search is feasible. We force an unused direction by counting repeated directions in the planes through a card on many sets, and treat configurations containing a magic square separately.

title: Zariski Topology of (Krasner) Hypermodules
authors: Behnam Afshar, Reza Ameri, Hashem Bordbar
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18726v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative Krasner hyperring with identity and $M$ an $R$-hypermodule. We consider the prime spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}_R(M)$, consisting of all prime subhypermodules of $M$. In this paper, we introduce a Zariski topology on $\operatorname{Spec}_R(M)$ and investigate its fundamental topological properties, including irreducibility, connectedness, compactness, and separation axioms, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for each. In particular, we prove that $\operatorname{Spec}_R(M)$ is irreducible if and only if the nilradical of $M$ is a prime hyperideal, and that it is connected precisely when the underlying hyperring is not a nontrivial direct product. We further investigate the functoriality of the Zariski topology in the category of Krasner hyperrings and hypermodules. Moreover, using the fundamental relation $\epsilon^{*}$, the smallest regular relation on $M$ for which the quotient $\overline{M}=M/\epsilon^{*}$ becomes an $\overline{R}=R/\Gamma^{*}$-module, we establish a correspondence between the Zariski topologies of $M$ and $\overline{M}$. We show that this correspondence is functorial and thereby relate the hypermodule-theoretic setting to the classical theory of modules over rings.

title: Support recovery of diffusion models under the manifold hypothesis
authors: Ayya Alieva, Gautam Iyer, Alexei Novikov, Lenya Ryzhik
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18738v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study diffusion models under the manifold hypothesis with possibly large score estimation and discretization errors, and show that while they may not exactly recover the data distribution, they will exactly recover the support (or data manifold). In continuous time, we use a Lyapunov function to show that even if the relative score estimation error is fixed (and not necessarily vanishing), then the rate at which the process approaches the support is $O(\sqrt{(T-t)|\log(T-t)|})$ as $t \to T$, where $T$ is the final time. In discrete time, we use geometric time steps with a fixed (non-vanishing) ratio and show that with a fixed (also not small) relative score estimation error, the process approaches the data manifold exponentially with the number of iterations. The proof relies on controlling a Gaussian measure of a neighborhood of the cut-locus of the data manifold, using a polynomial approximation argument combined with quantitative semi-algebraic estimates.

title: Two-Sided Projection-Based Model Reduction of Parametric Generalized Algebraic Riccati Equations via Grassmann-Manifold Optimization
authors: Xuelian Wen, Qiuqi Li, Juan Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18739v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Parametric generalized algebraic Riccati equations arise in many-query problems in optimal control, state estimation, and filtering, where repeated full-order solutions may become computationally prohibitive for large-scale systems. In this paper, within a projection-based model reduction framework, we propose a two-sided projection approach that constructs reduced bases by minimizing the aggregate relative two-sided projection error of Riccati solution snapshots. Under suitable dissipativity assumptions, the resulting Galerkin-projected PGARE admits a unique symmetric positive semidefinite stabilizing solution. For error assessment, we employ an existing residual-based a posteriori error estimator for the full-order Riccati residual. A projection-based error decomposition developed in this work provides the theoretical motivation for the proposed basis construction. To accommodate clustered solution manifolds, we extend the framework to localized model reduction by combining parameter-space proximity and solution-space correlation for clustering, with classifier-based online basis selection. Numerical experiments on parameterized heat-conduction problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed global and localized approaches in terms of approximation accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Minimality of the Double Kite among Strict Two-Pole Configurations of Unit Triangles
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18742v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A strict unit-triangle configuration is a finite connected family of closed equilateral unit triangles in which distinct triangles are disjoint or meet at a common vertex, and no vertex belongs to more than two triangles. A vertex belonging to exactly one triangle is a pole. We prove that every strict configuration with one or two poles contains at least fourteen triangles, a sharp bound for two poles attained by the double kite and the reverse double kite. A strict four-regular configuration whose contact graph has an edge cut of size at most two contains at least twenty-eight triangles. A decomposition into three strict two-pole components requires forty-two triangles; both known ring constructions attain the bound. The proof reduces minimal counterexamples to two-connected contact graphs, applies area bounds to complementary unit-sided polygons, and excludes the remaining cases by exact angle certificates. The supplement contains 13,668 stored marked records, 233 exclusion certificates, a standard-library verifier, and independent checks of the complete enumeration.

title: Lower semicontinuity of dimension for quasi-Bernoulli measures under conformal projections
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18752v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the dependence of the Hausdorff dimension of projected quasi-Bernoulli measures on a conformal iterated function system on the real line. For every fixed quasi-Bernoulli probability measure on the symbolic space, we prove that the dimension of its push-forward under the coding map is lower semicontinuous in the $C^{1+\theta}$ topology, without any separation assumption or shift-invariance requirement on the symbolic measure. The proof combines bounded distortion and finite-scale entropy estimates with uniform control of the entropy dimension over measures whose densities are bounded above and below. For invariant Gibbs measures associated with H\"older continuous potentials, we also prove joint lower semicontinuity with respect to the defining system and the potential. As an application, we obtain a generic dimension formula: for each fixed shift-invariant quasi-Bernoulli measure, a dense $G_\delta$ set of systems with derivative moduli strictly less than 1/2 has projected dimension equal to the minimum of one and the entropy-to-Lyapunov-exponent ratio.

title: Field algebras associated with non-symmetric lattices
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18762v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields. We associate to every finite-rank lattice $L$ equipped with an arbitrary bilinear form a canonical field algebra $V_L$, generalizing the Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras. We then study potential definitions of commutants in this setting and analyze when they are realized as subfield algebras. Finally, we realize these constructions geometrically by looking at the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending previous results from Dominic Joyce.

title: An ODE to Changing Variables: $v = y/x$ Is For Victory
authors: Joseph Kraisler, Kayla S. Miller, Steven J. Miller
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18764v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most first courses in differential equations introduce students to very special differential equations which can be solved in closed form from a small set of techniques (such as separable equations and integrating factors). Frequently other equations can be converted to one of these forms through a change of variable; however, these transformations are usually just given without any explanation of \emph{how} people found them, or \emph{why} problems of these forms have nice solutions, but not related ones. We consider the first order differential equation $dy/dx = f(x,y)$ where $f(x,y)$ does not factor as $A(x)B(y)$, and assume $f(x,y) = g(y/x^r)$ for some nice function $g$ and some real number $r$. This can be reduced to a separable equation only when $r=1$. We then discuss generalizations and what conditions on $f$ lead to a change of variables yielding a separable equation. Our goals are twofold. First, to encourage students and instructors to be active, questioning the methods and results, seeing how far they can be extended and why they work. Second, we discuss how to appropriately use AI to take ideas and special cases as prompts and quickly create extensions and editable notes that can be shared with students, freeing up professors (and students) from straightforward calculations \emph{without} sacrificing learning and understanding.

title: Self-adjoint boundary conditions for equation-free multiscale modelling
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18788v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Equation-free modelling is a computation multiscale modelling scheme for the simulation of complex dynamical systems. Efficient computations are achieved by solving the given microscale model in small, well-separated `patches' spread across the space-time domain, with each patch providing a data point for the macroscale simulation. Patch coupling bridges the unsimulated space between patches and supports the macroscale dynamics. Accurate simulations require coupling conditions that preserve underlying symmetries of the microscale equation. Failing to preserve such symmetries may result in an unphysical macroscale simulation that does not satisfy required conservation laws. Here we develop equation-free modelling that preserves self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models defined by a compact self-adjoint operator on a bounded domain with fixed boundary conditions. This new design for equation-free modelling greatly increases the range of systems for which equation-free modelling is applicable.

title: A proof of the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture on entropy maximization for cube projections
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18798v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We complete the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture: among the one-dimensional projections of the uniform measure on a cube, differential entropy is maximized precisely in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. Pang proved the conjecture in every dimension at least $150$. We prove the remaining dimensions using polynomial entropy bounds in dimensions three through six and exact certificates for derivatives of the logarithm of the diagonal projection density. The proof uses integer arithmetic and certified one-dimensional integration. We also derive quantitative stability estimates and determine the optimal asymptotic coefficient of a linear stability bound. The source code and the outputs of all finite verifications accompany the paper.

title: Invariant measures with uniform projection on surfaces and billiards
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18817v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study probability measures on the unit tangent bundle which are invariant under the geodesic flow and whose projection to the base manifold is the normalized Riemannian volume. We show that the Liouville measure is the only such measure on a complete oriented surface of finite area with ergodic geodesic flow. In particular, this resolves a conjecture of Katok--Knieper--Weiss in dimension two. The same holds for ergodic planar billiards with piecewise C2 boundary, such as the Bunimovich stadium, the Sinai billiard, and generic polygons. The proof combines the Fourier analysis in the fibers with holomorphic functions on the transport twistor space.
  As a consequence, on these surfaces and on the Bunimovich stadium, a high-energy sequence of normalized Laplacian eigenfunctions tends to be equidistributed in the phase space if and only if it tends to be equidistributed in the physical space. In particular, on every stadium, every failure of equidistribution in the phase space implies scarring in the physical space. Combined with Hassell's theorem, this gives a new proof of scarring in the physical space for almost every stadium.
  In higher dimensions, we obtain an entropy bound for the ergodic components of such measures. We also construct counterexamples for hyperbolic toral automorphisms.

title: Quasi-product and multiplicative Markov measures Radon-Nikodym problem, random walks: the free group case
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18853v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is a conceptual clarification of the role of a special class of measures on topological Markov chains - multiplicative Markov measures - in the context of random walks. It is achieved by combining the interpretation of multiplicative Markov measures on the boundary of a free group as the unique solutions of the Radon - Nikodym problem for product cocycles of the boundary action and the fact that the Radon - Nikodym cocycle of the harmonic measure of a nearest neighbour random walk on a free group is a product one.

title: Global Lanczos with stochastic error correction for trace estimation of matrix functions
authors: Michele Rinelli, Igor Simunec, Robbe Vermeiren
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18864v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a new method for computing the trace of a matrix function $f(A)$, where $A$ is a large, sparse, symmetric matrix. Our approach combines a deterministic global Lanczos approximation with a stochastic correction of its error. Starting the global Lanczos process with the identity matrix yields a direct approximation of the trace through a small tridiagonal matrix. The resulting basis matrices are polynomials in $A$, allowing the process to be implemented using sparse matrix-matrix multiplications when low-degree polynomials in $A$ have moderate fill-in. However, increased fill-in may limit the number of iterations that can be performed efficiently. To address this limitation, we derive an exact representation of the global Lanczos error as the trace of a matrix function and apply a stochastic estimator to the remainder. Even a moderately accurate estimate can substantially improve the accuracy, combining the deterministic method with the rapid initial convergence of stochastic trace estimators. We discuss error bounds and variance reduction, and present numerical experiments that compare the resulting method with existing ones.

title: Spectral Conditioning of Weighted Multivariate Vandermonde Operators via Radial Beurling--Selberg Approximation
authors: Joseph Gabet, Maxime Ferreira Da Costa, Kiryung Lee
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18900v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish explicit eigenvalue bounds for Gram matrices of weighted multivariate Vandermonde operators with separated nodes on a torus. The squared magnitudes of the weights are samples of a nonnegative radial spectral energy density whose profile has bounded variation, finite energy, and finite weighted variation cost; compact support is not required. The estimate holds in every dimension and depends on the periodic Euclidean separation and the weighted variation integral. For compactly supported profiles, our analysis combines a signed layer decomposition with the ball approximants of Holt and Vaaler; the noncompactly supported case follows by truncation. Combining the resulting radial envelopes with a bandlimited sampling identity based on Poisson summation yields the spectral bounds by eliminating off-diagonal interactions and nonzero diagonal aliases. The result covers nonmonotone profiles and discontinuous radial low-pass filters, and it is complemented by a global elementary upper bound on the Holt--Vaaler cost that exhibits two radial regimes.

title: Discrete Hyperbolic Cosecant Distributions
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18913v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce three families of discrete hyperbolic cosecant probability distributions, supported either bilaterally on $\mathbb{Z}$ or unilaterally on $\mathbb{N}_0$, inspired by series evaluations of Srinivasa Ramanujan. We determine their exact normalization constants in terms of singular values of complete elliptic integrals and the Gau\ss ian constant $G=\varpi/\pi$ with the lemniscate constant $\Gamma^2(1/4)/(2\sqrt{2\pi})$ by explicitly calculating some series, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{\kappa \in \mathbb{Z}} 2\kappa \operatorname{cosech}(\kappa \pi) = G^2 + \frac{1}{\pi}. $$ Furthermore, by connecting these distributions to Fourier transforms of powers of the hyperbolic secant and applying the Poisson summation formula, we obtain closed-form evaluations for even moments and hyperbolic secant lattice sums, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathrm{sech}^4(k \pi) = \frac{2}{3} \left(G^4 + G^2 + \frac{1}{\pi}\right). $$ This machinery proves conjectures on lattice sums arising in electrostatics proposed by Vigren and Dieckmann (Symmetry, 2020).

title: History independence and base-dominant rigidity for polynomial skew products
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18917v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study history independence of fast directions and its relation to the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula for regular polynomial skew products of degree $d\ge2$. Assuming uniform expansion on the support of the measure of maximal entropy and a base Lyapunov exponent larger than the vertical exponent, we prove that history independence is equivalent to conjugacy to a polynomial product by an affine shear map. Under history independence, the measure of maximal entropy satisfies the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula. If, in addition, the splitting is dominated, the dimension formula also implies history independence. The proof first upgrades the measurable fast direction to a holomorphic line field and then uses its invariance on periodic fibers to force the affine product structure. The converse dimension implication combines an entropy comparison argument with rigidity of local symmetries of periodic fiber Julia sets.

title: Dual-Mode Extremum Seeking for a Class of Unknown Controlled Diffusions
authors: Martin Guay, Shimin Wang, Edward Z. Cao, Stefan Damjanovic
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18923v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A dual-mode extremum-seeking controller is developed for unknown nonlinear systems with affine control inputs driven by persistent Brownian process noise. The controller uses a single measured cost, without state estimation or differentiation of the measurement. Bounded cosine feedback generates, through Lie-bracket averaging, a proportional--integral (PI) action: the proportional action stabilizes a feasible minimum of the cost on the time scale of the plant, and the integral action adapts a bias toward the unknown input that regulates the plant at that minimum. The averaged closed loop is a PI-regulated diffusion that retains the process noise, and its stability condition does not require knowledge of the control direction. Under a regional Lyapunov condition on the averaged dynamics, an exact periodic response of the noise-free closed loop is constructed and serves as the center of a Lyapunov function with bounds uniform in the excitation frequency. Exit-probability estimates show that, for small noise and large excitation frequency, trajectories reach a prescribed neighborhood of the optimum and remain there for times exponential in the inverse noise variance, with exponentially small failure probability. Under an additional stochastic contraction condition, the closed loop is approximated uniformly in time, in mean square before common exit, by its averaged diffusion driven by the same Brownian motion, with an error that decreases with the excitation frequency. The regional regulation conditions are verified for a planar hydrodynamic trap with an unknown stagnation-point offset and actuator sign. Simulations illustrate intensity-only confinement of a Brownian particle, integral compensation of the holding input, and axial-strip exit statistics.

title: Compromise Optimization over Incompatible Efficient Sets Using a Minimax Distance Approach with Polyhedral Characterization and an Application to Fisheries Management
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18932v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The efficient sets associated with different decision-makers may have an empty intersection, even when their objectives are linear and the common feasible region is a compact polytope. In this paper, we consider a compromise criterion that minimizes the largest weighted distance from a feasible decision to the respective efficient sets of the decision-makers. First, we establish the existence of an optimal compromise and show that the formulation recovers the common efficient set whenever it is nonempty. We then derive a lower bound based on the separation of efficient sets and obtain an exact formulation in terms of finitely many linear programs by exploiting their polyhedral structure. Next, we examine the effect of approximating the efficient sets and establish a stability bound expressed in terms of the Hausdorff distance. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of the proposed approach through a numerical study of harvest allocation between two interconnected fishing zones.

title: Surrogate Symbols in Wireless Communications
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Co-channel interference (CCI), caused by the inevitable aggressive channel reuse in dense deployments, remains a critical bottleneck for current and future wireless communication systems. In this paper, we address this bottleneck in an N-co-channel wireless communications network of single-antenna transmitters and receivers. The limiting case of this problem leads to a novel "thought experiment": If each receiver's own desired channel link is simultaneously completely blocked, can a Maximum Likelihood Detection at each receiver still recover its transmitted symbol? In the traditional way of thinking, the answer is no: The receiver obtains nothing but co-channel interference (CCI) plus thermal noise, and a receiver-side phase rotation cannot help, since there is no desired signal to align. Given only the channel matrix H -- and no knowledge of the transmitted symbols -- can the transmitters' phases be chosen so that the received signal becomes "almost" the desired symbol at every receiver? We show that the answer is yes. We first develop the underlying framework for the general case (nonzero own-channel link case), turning classical co-channel systems into a novel discrete phase-optimization problem, "Game of Phases: Surrogate Symbol Optimization", and present two algorithms, "Minimum Phased-Interference Power algorithm (MiPIP)" and "Maximum Phased-Interference Support (MaPRIS)". We then show that the MaPRIS resolves the thought experiment: it converts hostile CCI into an "almost" desired symbol even when the own desired channel link is zero, yielding the counter-intuitive result that higher CCI variance yields higher SINR. Extensive simulation results confirm the findings. The gain promised by the proposed algorithms comes on top of any other CCI reduction techniques as our framework here is based on a bottom-line baseband model.

title: A Fast and Accurate Time-Space Decomposition for Unit Commitment With Storage
authors: Chance Brainard, Kylind Reagan, Shaked Regev
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18946v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Grid-scale batteries couple decisions across time. This makes unit commitment (UC) with thousands of buses, batteries, generators, and alternating current constraints intractable. We introduce a time-space decomposition (TSD) heuristic to solve the problem. We first calculate target net battery charge or discharge rates on a zonal level, relaxing spatial constraints. We then incorporate this target into the Relax-and-Round UC (RRUC) solver from our previous work. RRUC enforces the spatial transmission constraints and transfers power between zones, if that reduces costs. We show that our TSD produces an error of about 0.1% on a simpler economic dispatch problem with batteries. This is larger than the error produced by RRUC in the tests in our previous work. So, we conjecture that the combined error of our two approximations is not much larger than 0.1%. We show that TSD with RRUC can solve systems with 10,000 buses in about 6 minutes, with sub-quadratic scaling, making it suitable for real time operations on an ISO-sized system.

title: Joint Channel Estimation, Data Detection, and Phase Noise Tracking in Massive MIMO Systems
authors: Toan-Van Nguyen, Duy H. N. Nguyen
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18947v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Communication over multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems is degraded by phase noise (PN) arising from imperfect local oscillators, with PN becoming more severe at higher carrier frequencies. Existing methods either rely on linearized Kalman-filter approaches or apply variational Bayes (VB) only to individual stages, such as data detection under a static phase prior, or channel estimation alone, leaving no unified framework that tracks an evolving PN process consistently across pilot and data transmission. This paper develops such a framework for uplink massive MIMO. Specifically, we first propose VB-Tracking, which employs von Mises priors and coordinate-ascent VB inference to jointly estimate the channel and track the transmit and receive PN trajectories during the pilot phase without linearization. We then propose VB-Detecting for joint data detection and phase tracking by absorbing the transmit PN into a composite transmit variable. Using a sequentially propagated von Mises predictive prior, the composite variable admits an exact closed-form posterior. Finally, we propose VB-Refining, which periodically re-estimates the channel during data transmission using the soft posterior moments of reliably detected transmit symbols as virtual pilots. We show that VB-Detecting scales linearly in the number of users, receive antennas, constellation size, and iterations. Simulations against EKF-EP, EKF-ZF, and JED baselines show that VB-Tracking, VB-Detecting, and VB-Refining together achieve lower channel NMSE and symbol error rate, with the performance gap widening at high SNR and under severe PN.

title: NeRI: Neural Residual Iteration for Elliptic Operator Equations and Variational Inequalities
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18992v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work, we propose a so-called {\it Neural Residual Iteration} (NeRI), a weak-form neural-network framework for solving a class of elliptic operator equations and variational inequalities, including nonlinear and nonsymmetric problems that may not admit a global energy functional. The key idea is to construct, at each iteration, a state-dependent linear functional whose derivative with respect to the trial function recovers the current weak residual. A single gradient step is then performed on the residual, yielding a residual-driven neural update without requiring a global energy functional or an additional test network. From a function-space perspective, NeRI can be interpreted as a neural-tangent-kernel-preconditioned realization of classical residual iterations, thereby bridging classical iterative solvers and neural-network optimization. We further extend NeRI to elliptic variational inequalities (VIs) through penalized and constraint-preserving formulations. For wide two-layer networks under gradient flow, we prove finite-time lazy-training estimates and derive an $H^1$-error decomposition relative to the exact weak solution. Numerical experiments on several elliptic problems demonstrate the effectiveness of NeRI, particularly for nonsymmetric and low-regularity problems.

title: Zero area of quartic Fibonacci Julia sets
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18993v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the Julia set of the degree-four Fibonacci renormalization 2-periodic point has zero planar Lebesgue measure. As a corollary, the degree four Fibonacci polynomial $z^4+c_{\mathrm{Fib}}$ has zero measure Julia set.

title: Averaged-Cost Control with Shared Feedback under Model Uncertainty
authors: Piernicola Bettiol, Daisuke Inoue, Mat\'ias G\'omez-Aedo, Dante Kalise, Richard B. Vinter
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19019v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper studies the shared-feedback design problem for finite-horizon averaged-cost control under model uncertainty represented by a joint law over the model parameter and initial state. One feedback map is shared across all realizations and uses only time and the current state as online inputs. We develop two methods: the nonlinear adjoint method combines forward closed-loop solves, backward adjoints, and joint-law policy gradients, while the linear moment method gives exact cost and gradient formulas for a homogeneous linear-quadratic design model by propagating conditional second moments. Numerical studies compare averaged and nominal designs for time-dependent neural feedback and static linear feedback in nonlinear Van der Pol and Stuart-Landau systems; the static gains are designed from oscillator linearizations and evaluated on the original nonlinear systems. Averaged design has lower cost in most comparisons.

title: Spherical functions of the quantum symmetric pair of type FII
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19024v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove Schl\"osser's conjecture relating quantum FII spherical functions to Askey--Wilson polynomials for equal left and right coideal parameters and determine the corresponding radial operator. An explicit transport formula gives the shifted restrictions for arbitrary nonzero parameters.

title: Optimal Capital Injections in a Microlending Group under External Shocks
authors: H\'ector Jasso-Fuentes, Alejandra Quintos, Xinta Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19028v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Motivated by static models of group default in microlending, we study a dynamic problem in which the members of a lending group are exposed to external shocks, such as droughts or floods, and the manager of a common emergency fund decides at each shock how much capital to inject into the members who were hit. Shocks arrive at random times, the set of members that a shock hits may depend on which members the previous shock hit, and the losses may spill over to members who were not hit directly. Between shocks, the members' wealth follows a linear stochastic differential equation in which members support each other, and the fund grows with interest and member contributions up to a cap. The cost balances the members' shortfall below a poverty line, a welfare measure that contains a standard poverty measure as a special case, against the administrative cost of the injections and the benefit of keeping money in the fund. We formulate the problem as a Markov decision process embedded at the shock times and prove that the embedded process is Markov with a weakly continuous transition kernel. When the discount rate exceeds a growth rate determined by the wealth dynamics, we show that the expected total cost is finite under every policy, that the finite-horizon optimal values converge to the infinite-horizon one at an explicit rate, and that there exists a stationary optimal injection policy, which can be chosen independent of calendar time.

title: Delay Closure of Observable Dynamics for the Heat Equation
authors: Xiaoting Han, Dongbin Xiu, Ludmil T. Zikatanov
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19040v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study finite-delay representations of point observables, which are solution values at selected spatial locations, for spatially discretized heat equations. We show that the observables satisfy closed dynamical systems whose evolution depends only on their own history, without requiring solution values elsewhere in the domain. Using semigroup properties, we analyze low-rank approximate closures that can use substantially fewer delay terms than the exact representation. We consider two computational approaches: direct least-squares fitting of delay coefficients from observable trajectories and shift-invert Krylov approximation of the semigroup using preconditioned linear solves. Numerical experiments for constant- and variable-coefficient heat equations in one, two, and three dimensions illustrate the effects of memory length and sensor information on prediction. The results are consistent with the theoretical analysis.

title: Learning-Enhanced Reduce-Repair-Refine-Optimize Framework for Real-Time Train Platforming
authors: Md Tabish Haque, Sebastian Sehmisch, Christopher Szymula, Nikola Be\v{s}inovi\'c
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19041v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Real-time train platforming under disruptions requires rapid revision of routing, platforming, and timing decisions. Dense traffic and shared infrastructure create tightly coupled conflicts, making real-time optimization computationally demanding. This paper proposes a learning-enhanced Reduce-Repair-Refine-Optimize framework that reduces and selectively relaxes the routing search space to balance computational efficiency, feasibility, and solution quality. The reduction stage constructs a restricted MILP by fixing selected routing decisions using route-specific predictive models and thresholds, thereby accounting for heterogeneity across routes. Two adaptive mechanisms subsequently modify the reduced search space: repair selectively releases route fixings to restore feasibility, while refinement releases additional fixings to recover routing alternatives and improve solution quality without reverting to the unrestricted problem. Computational experiments on real-life disrupted station-area instances show that the framework matches or improves upon a recent rTPP heuristic in more than 80% of instances within 60~s. Under the common 180~s budget, the framework obtains strictly better terminal incumbents than the unrestricted MILP in 56.7% of all instances and 77.4% of hard instances. Moreover, it obtains better terminal incumbents than an otherwise identical variant without refinement in 71.9% of hard instances. The results demonstrate that learning-based search-space reduction is most effective when the reduced search space remains adaptable during optimization, enabling high-quality feasible solutions within the real-time computation budget.

title: Log-optimal two-sample testing by betting
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19062v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For each standard Borel observation space, we construct a single anytime-valid two-sample procedure that is asymptotically log-optimal for every pair of unknown probability laws and every limiting ratio of diverging sample sizes, including zero and infinity. For independent balanced pairs, the optimal log-wealth rate is $2\JS(P,Q)$, where $\JS$ is the Jensen--Shannon divergence. Unequal sizes yield weighted Jensen--Shannon information and the one-sample limit $\log W(n_1,n_2)/n_2\to\KL(Q\|P)$ when $n_1/n_2\to\infty$. Refining finite partitions and logarithmic-loss learning with measurable characteristic kernels provide universal constructions. Our main contribution is the generality of our construction, and its connections to classical batch efficiency notions. Practical implementations allow continuous classifier fine-tuning, as demonstrated on finite alphabets, Gaussian data, and handwritten digits.

title: New constructions of optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for quasi-block monotone Ferrers diagrams
authors: Yong Jin, Yuhao Ning, Dengming Xu, Chengming Duan
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19070v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Constant dimension subspace codes (CDCs) have become an important object in coding theory due to their applications in random network coding. The paper is devoted to constructing optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for block Ferrers diagrams, which play a crucial role in the multilevel construction of CDCs. Let \(\mathbb{F}_q\) be the finite field with \(q\) elements of characteristic \(p\), \(P\) be a power of \(p\), and \(e\) be a positive integer. Let \(L=\mathbb F_{q^{eP}}\) and \(\sigma\) be the Frobenius \(\mathbb F_q\)-automorphism of \(L\), set \(N=\sigma^e-\mathrm{id}\). Based on the multiplicative property of the kernel filtration of the nilpotent map \(N\), we construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for block monotone diagrams. Specifically, considering \(n \times l\) Ferrers diagrams, we prove that optimal codes always exist for block monotone diagrams when \(n = eP\). Furthermore, by employing puncturing on columns, we prove that optimal codes also always exist for block strictly monotone diagrams, removing the restriction \(n = eP\). Consequently, optimal codes always exist for block upper triangular diagrams, specifically for maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD)-constructible block diagram pairs, which generalizes the corresponding results in \cite{neri2024,calderini2026}, in which the rank distance or the characteristic is restricted. Furthermore, by employing both puncturing and shortening on columns, we prove that optimal codes always exist for quasi-block strictly monotone diagrams, thereby generalizing the corresponding results in \cite{pratihar2023, zhang2019}. The optimal codes constructed in this paper will potentially be beneficial to the further construction of CDCs.

title: Pole rigidity in root-optimal rational approximation of the exponential on infinite sectors
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19119v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The optimal root convergence factor for uniform rational approximation of the exponential on an infinite sector is classical. We prove that, for every fixed infinite sector of opening less than $\pi$, the normalized pole-counting measures of any reduced root-optimal sequence, after scaling the poles by degree, converge weakly to a uniquely determined probability measure supported on a compact analytic arc outside the sector. For the half-line, the corresponding pole law was previously announced by Stahl and Schmelzer; our new result covers sectors of positive opening. The proof rules out boundary pole accumulation and controls an exponentially small Hermite residual through reflection and noncancellation, without assuming interpolation or orthogonality. We explicitly construct the equilibrium measure and its supporting arc in terms of a zero of a Ferrers function, and relate this parameterization to the Gonchar--Rakhmanov theta equation. We also obtain a degree-independent comparison for simultaneous approximation of finitely many $\varphi$-functions with a common denominator. Numerical pole distributions support the theoretical law.

title: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
authors: Rathindra Nath Karmakar, Samriddha Lahiry, Koichi Yamagata
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19141v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter.
  As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

title: Mean-field Token Steering
authors: Md Zulfiqur Haider, Asmaa Eldesoukey, Abhishek Halder, Yongxin Chen
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19163v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider stochastic token steering through a deep stack of transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for an interacting particle system on the unit sphere, where interactions arise from the attention mechanism. In the mean-field limit, the token population evolves via a controlled integro-partial differential equation where the feedback control acts as a corrective vector field guiding the population toward an aggregate configuration of tokens in the representation space. We deduce the minimum effort control to accomplish this task over a fixed time horizon interpreted as normalized layer depth. We show that the resulting controlled dynamics for the token population can be understood as a mean-field Schr\"odinger bridge adapted to the sphere geometry. Building on this, we propose a novel generalization of the dynamic Sinkhorn recursion to compute the consistent token evolution. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed approach achieves exact steering of the token population.

title: Interpolation, Factorization, and Approximation in the Numerical Radius Unit Ball
authors: Hamidul Ahmed, Mainak Bhowmik, B. Krishna Das, Haripada Sau
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19189v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We initiate a systematic study of Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and function theory for matrix-valued holomorphic functions on the unit disk taking values in the numerical radius unit ball - a class we term as $
u$-Schur functions.
  In contrast to the operator-norm setting, where commutatnt lifting reduces interpolation to the positivity of a single Pick matrix, we show that a natural one-parameter familty of Pick-type matrices arising from Ando's characterization is necessary but not sufficient for solvability. We overcome this obstruction by establishing two necessary and sufficient solvability criteria. The first is constructive, resting on a factorization of $
u$-Schur function $F=PGQ$ into a classical Schur function $G$ and bounded holomorphic matrix functions $P, Q$ coupled by a boundary condition. This yields an accompanying Choi-Li-type dilation representation. The second is dual and geometric, characterizing solvability via a Nehari-type distance from a cononical model-space interpolant to a subspace determined by the interpolation data.
  Finally, we introduce $
u$-inner functions - $
u$-Schur functions whose non-tangential boundary values lie almost everywhere in the set of extremal numerical contractions - and prove that every non-extremal problem admits a $
u$-inner solution. As a consequence, we obtain a numerical-radius Caratheodory approximation theorem: $
u$-inner functions are dense in the $
u$-Schur class under the compact-open topology.

title: Intersection Cuts for Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programs via Decision-Diagram-Free Sets
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19197v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce a novel decision-diagram-based framework for generating intersection cuts to strengthen polyhedral relaxations of bounded mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) with general nonlinear constraints. Building on decision diagrams (DDs) that provide outer approximations of MINLP feasible regions, we propose the concept of DD-free sets, which are convex regions whose interiors do not intersect the sets represented by the DDs. By exploiting the underlying graphical structure, we develop efficient methods for constructing these regions without requiring restrictive assumptions on the functional form of nonlinear constraints or access to distance oracles. We investigate the maximality properties of DD-free sets and devise algorithms for obtaining maximal forbidden regions within several structured classes. The resulting intersection cuts exploit geometric information retained in DD representations, enabling further strengthening of relaxations beyond what can be achieved through conventional DD-based convexification. We also introduce interval DDs to facilitate the representation of general nonlinear constraints and establish convergence results for intersections of constraint-specific DDs, providing a theoretical foundation for their integration into global optimization frameworks. Computational experiments on challenging open instances from MINLPLib, encompassing a broad range of nonlinear and nonconvex structures, demonstrate that the proposed approach can substantially improve dual bounds and achieve greater optimality-gap closure than state-of-the-art global optimization solvers. These findings highlight the potential of exploiting graphical representations of infeasible regions to develop stronger cutting planes for general MINLPs.

title: Learning the Average Dose-Response Function with a Right-Censored Treatment
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19204v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper considers estimation and inference for the average dose-response function under right-censored treatment duration and missing outcomes for censored units. Using the duration lower bounds provided by censored records, we construct a novel multiply robust estimator through augmented local estimating equations. Under suitable regularity conditions, the estimator remains consistent when any two of the outcome regression, treatment density, and censoring survival function are consistently estimated. We establish its convergence rate and asymptotic distribution within a cross-fitting framework under appropriate conditions on nuisance estimation. To address local smoothing bias that can distort confidence interval coverage, we further develop a debiased estimator that supports asymptotically valid pointwise inference without undersmoothing. Under additional uniform conditions, we construct simultaneous confidence bands using a Gaussian multiplier bootstrap. Simulation studies evaluate estimation accuracy, the validity of pointwise and uniform inference, and robustness to nuisance model misspecification. A semi-synthetic study calibrated to NHANES illustrates the proposed methods in a setting with a known dose-response function.

title: Martingale and signed diffusive optimal transport: geodesics and gradient flows
authors: Aymeric Baradat, Jean-David Benamou, Fran\c{c}ois-Xavier Vialard
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In signed diffusive transport, a path of probability densities $\rho_t$ on the circle and a momentum $m_t$ satisfy $\partial_t\rho=\partial_{xx}m$, and the cost of the path is the action $\int_0^1\int m^2/(2\rho)\,dx\,dt$. The diffusivity $m/\rho$ is an unknown of this variational problem and can take either sign. On the real line, the constraint $m\ge0$ gives the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem of Huesmann and Trevisan. We study geodesics and minimizing movements, which discretize gradient flows. For signed geodesics, we prove the $\Gamma$-convergence of the time-discrete problems for all probability endpoints, and of the fully discrete Fourier-grid problems as the space and time meshes tend to zero independently, without a positive lower bound on the densities. For a modified Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme on the torus, we prove convergence along subsequences to a weak solution of a fourth-order equation, the Derrida-Lebowitz-Speer-Spohn equation for the entropy in dimension one, under the assumption that the densities of the scheme stay above a positive constant on every finite time interval. In dimension one, the normalized minimum values of a discretization with nonnegative momentum and of a discretization by martingale couplings with a fourth-moment cost converge to the same martingale transport cost, and we identify the limit of the minimizing movements with nonnegative momentum for potential energies with bounded second and third derivatives. We compute geodesics and modified JKO trajectories by Douglas-Rachford splitting and by an interior-point method, and bound the optimization errors of selected solutions by dual lower bounds evaluated in interval arithmetic. The computed geodesics approach zero density near the points where the diffusivity changes sign, and along computed trajectories of the modified JKO scheme the density minimum can fall below its initial value.

title: Spectral Gaps and Low-Energy Modes in Anisotropic High-Contrast PDEs
authors: Yajun Wang, Eric T. Chung, Lijian Jiang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19235v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the low-energy spectrum of high-contrast partial differential equations with strongly anisotropic inclusions. The inclusion stiffness and mass are scaled by a contrast parameter \(\eta\), while a small material eigenvalue \(\epsilon\) controls anisotropy. Stable extensions of local kernel fields give eigenvalue upper bounds proportional to the inverse contrast, uniformly in anisotropy. Additional low-energy modes arise from fields whose nonzero differential images lie in weak material directions. Each fixed family of compatible weak fields yields additional eigenvalue upper bounds of order $\epsilon+ \eta^{-1}$, provided a stable extension exists. Under discrete stability assumptions, we obtain corresponding finite element bounds for the weak modes represented by the mesh. For separable scalar diffusion, we prove norm-resolvent convergence to independent background Dirichlet and inclusion Neumann operators as contrast tends to infinity with anisotropy fixed. Numerical experiments for four PDE models illustrate weak modes and mesh-dependent spectral transitions, and scalar diffusion experiments also test spectral decoupling and eigenvalue counting.

title: Veech dichotomy for specific covering surface over Veech surface
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19243v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: It is known that Veech dichotomy, which states that minimal directions are uniquely ergodic, holds for Veech surface and covering surface branched at a single non-periodic connection point of Veech surface. We give a sufficient condition for Veech dichotomy holds for a finite translation cover of a Veech surface, and applies it on branched cover of square-tiled surfaces to construct examples that satisfy Veech dichotomy but aren't Veech surfaces.

title: Many faces of integer semidefinite programming
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19255v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We first establish several properties of integer positive semidefinite matrices, extending known results for binary and ternary positive semidefinite matrices. We then show how to reformulate an integer quadratic program (IQP) as an equivalent integer semidefinite program (ISDP). We distinguish three cases, namely IQPs with two, three, or more than three distinct integer values, and provide several ISDPs for each case. Each reformulation yields either a binary ISDP, a ternary ISDP, or a rescaled version of one of these. The results show that ternary SDP formulations for problems with three distinct integer values provide SDP relaxations with fewer constraints and, in the case of equally spaced integers, also smaller matrix variables than binary-based SDP relaxations. For quadratic problems whose variables can take more than three distinct integer values, one can choose among three formulations based on the size of their matrix variables, the number of constraints, and the strength of the resulting SDP relaxations. We also show how to reformulate a mixed-integer QP as a mixed-integer SDP.

title: Multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for Banach space valued holomorphic functions
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19268v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study a generalized notion of multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for holomorphic functions defined on the unit ball of the finite-dimensional Minkowski sequence space with values in complex Banach spaces. We first prove that the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius is positive for every non-null bounded linear operator whose norm is sufficiently small relative to the scaling parameter. We then determine the exact asymptotic behavior of the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces of finite cotype and we obtain analogous bounds for spaces without finite cotype. Finally, for concave Banach lattices and summing operators, we prove lower bounds that involve a logarithmic factor. These results connect classical scalar Bohr phenomena with operator-valued and Banach space valued settings, and highlight how the geometry of the spaces and the mapping properties of the operator influence coefficient estimates and their dependence on dimension. Several examples illustrate the consistency of our results with the classical Bohr radius and the sharp Defant--Frerick asymptotics.

title: Entropy-Based and Quadratic Conditional Innovation Metrics for Informed Dynamic Scheduling of Belief-Propagation Decoding for LDPC Codes
authors: Tofar Chih-Yuan Chang, Chia-En Liu, Ying-Ren Jian, Di-Chun Liang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19269v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose two enhanced conditional innovation (CI) metrics for informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) in belief-propagation (BP) decoding of LDPC codes. The CI-based residual BP (CIRBP) algorithm uses the CI metric to guide the selection of the variable node (VN) to be updated and has been shown to outperform several existing IDS-based BP decoders, especially at the early decoding stage. However, the original CI metric uses only the absolute difference between the current and precomputed posterior probabilities and does not separately account for the reliability associated with each probability. By reformulating the CI metric relative to the decision boundary, we separate each posterior probability into its decision side and a linear-distance term reflecting reliability. Replacing the latter with the binary entropy complement yields the proposed entropy-based CI (E-CI) metric. Moreover, the proposed quadratic CI (Q-CI) metric is derived from the leading quadratic term in the local expansion of the entropy complement, avoiding the logarithmic operations required for direct E-CI evaluation. We apply both proposed metrics to the CIRBP decoder and its node-wise variant. Numerical results show that the proposed metrics generally provide lower frame error rates than the original CI metric, with their relative advantages depending on the code and decoding procedure.

title: An all-steps-at-once algorithm for time-domain wave propagation in heterogeneous and unbounded media
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19288v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose, analyze, and implement a convolution quadrature (CQ) algorithm for transient acoustic waves in an unbounded medium consisting of a heterogeneous domain embedded in free space, where the wave speed may be spatially variable and discontinuous. Multistep CQ, applied to the time-domain solution operator, reduces the evolution problem to a family of Helmholtz problems with damped complex frequencies, which can be solved independently in parallel, all time steps at once. The frequency problems are discretized by an overlapping coupling of finite elements (FEM) on a polygonal/polyhedral domain containing the inhomogeneity, and boundary elements (BEM) on a smooth curve enclosed by that domain, in the region where the medium is homogeneous, which accounts exactly for the unbounded exterior. Neither discretization needs to conform to the geometry of the heterogeneous domain, nor to each other.
  For the resulting FEM--BEM coupling we prove bounds for the solution operators of the transformed problems that are explicit in the Laplace parameter and the wave speed. These bounds yield convergence of the time discretization for A-stable multistep schemes. We also prove explicit estimates on the exponential decay of the transformed solutions away from the heterogeneity, which show that the correction provided by the BEM part is small but relevant, and cheap to compute: a few GMRES iterations suffice, and the correction is needed only over a fixed range of weakly damped frequencies, beyond which it becomes negligible and can be dropped. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates in time and space and explore iterative (multigrid) methods for the interior FEM problems.

title: Repairing actuator schedules under graph constraints
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19291v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider a discrete-time linear system in which each actuator is assigned to one time slot. A graph $H$ records which pairs of actuators cannot share a slot. We seek to remove conflicts by exchanging actuators between slots, while preserving all tail reachability spaces. These spaces describe the terminal corrections available from each time slot onward. We give a sufficient condition based on the number of exchanges that preserve the required bases. The condition guarantees repair from every compatible starting schedule. Two bounds for checking it use failed basis tests and dependent column selections. Each accepted exchange reduces the conflict count, so the procedure uses at most as many exchanges as there are initial conflicts. An explicit family with unequal rank increments admits repair when $3N>4\Delta(H)+4$, where $\Delta(H)$ is the largest number of forbidden partners of any actuator. We also give a family of two-slot examples with only one forbidden partner per actuator and two initial conflicts. The basis constraints force every strict improvement to move arbitrarily many actuators, although one exchange suffices without those constraints. A second example has a connected conflict graph and one initial conflict.

title: Fundamental Limits of Statistical Watermarking for LLMs with Fixed and Optimizable Common Randomness
authors: Haiyun He, Yepeng Liu, Zhuoer Shen, Ziqiao Wang, Yongyi Mao, Yuheng Bu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19305v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Watermarking has emerged as an important technique for distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written text. However, most existing work is primarily empirical, relies on ad hoc watermarking designs, and lacks a fundamental understanding of the performance limits. In this paper, we propose a unified theoretical framework for statistical watermarking of large language models (LLMs), casting the problem as an independence test between generated text and common randomness and jointly designing the watermarking embedder and the detector. Our objective is to maximize detection power while controlling the worst-case false positive rate (FPR) and limiting distortion to text quality. A central focus of our framework is the design of the common randomness, which plays a critical role in both watermark embedding and detection. We characterize the fundamental limits of statistical watermarking under both fixed and optimizable common randomness. Our results show that optimizing the common randomness does not improve the fundamental limits: the best achievable performance is the same as that with fixed common randomness. Nevertheless, common randomness design remains highly important because it can substantially simplify detector design. In particular, with optimizable common randomness, a fixed, deterministic, and model-agnostic detector can achieve optimal performance. We further study a practical setting with fixed uniform common randomness and a fixed deterministic detector, and characterize its performance gap relative to the optimizable case, thereby demonstrating the practical value of optimizable common randomness.

title: Structural latent dimension: deterministic geometry and local Fisher structure
abstract:
arXiv:2611.19322v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the \emph{structural dimension} of a second-order object: the minimum latent dimension that remains necessary relative to a declared class of competing dependence. Building on minimum-rank factor analysis and low-rank-plus-sparse decomposition, we use distances to lower-dimensional classes to describe inference near structural ambiguity. General distance and tangent-cone facts yield confidence statements and local margins. For rank-zero competitors with bounded residual degree, we derive exact maximum-weight $b$-matching formulas, support-slack tangent cones and sparse-spike angles; a shared residual support across a field can produce separation absent pointwise. We give positive-semidefinite brackets, a dimension-free Gaussian likelihood expansion, an exact quotient by the tangent of a low-rank background, and a detection floor from the margin. Equal-angle configurations with different branch multiplicities motivate static and spectral detection conjectures. Joint low-rank/residual profiling and the sharp composite information boundaries remain open.
